accepted.s: The Telangana Peasant Armed Struggle of 1946–1951 was directed primarily against which system of rule?
o: The feudal order of the Nizam in Hyderabad State
The ryotwari system of the Madras Presidency
accepted.x: The struggle in Hyderabad State was directed against the Nizam’s feudal order, particularly the power of jagirdars and deshmukhs and the practice of Vetti.
accepted.tq: Identify the central authority and the specific system against which the movement was directed.
accepted.sec: Telangana armed struggle - Komaraiah, Ailamma, Andhra Mahasabha presidents, leaders and memoirs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who among the following were associated with the leadership of the Telangana Peasant Armed Struggle on behalf of the Communist Party of India?
o: P. Sundarayya and Chandra Rajeswara Rao
accepted.x: P. Sundarayya and Chandra Rajeswara Rao were the principal CPI leaders associated with the Telangana armed struggle.
accepted.tq: Match the movement with its actual political leaders rather than leaders of similar peasant struggles.
accepted.sec: Telangana armed struggle - Komaraiah, Ailamma, Andhra Mahasabha presidents, leaders and memoirs  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Andhra Mahasabha:
1. It initially concentrated on cultural work.
2. During the 1930s and 1940s, it moved towards leftist agrarian politics.
3. By the 1940s, it functioned as the organisational front of the Communist Party of India in the Telangana struggle.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Andhra Mahasabha evolved from cultural activity into a left-oriented agrarian organisation and became the CPI’s organisational front in the struggle.
accepted.tq: Test the transformation of an organisation across time through a coded statement question.
accepted.sec: Telangana armed struggle - Komaraiah, Ailamma, Andhra Mahasabha presidents, leaders and memoirs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Doddi Komaraiah, regarded as the first martyr of the Telangana armed struggle, was shot at Kadavendi on 4 July 1946 by the men of which person?
accepted.x: Doddi Komaraiah was shot at Kadavendi in Jangaon on 4 July 1946 by the men of the Visnur deshmukh.
accepted.tq: Apply the wrong-person-with-the-deed trap to distinguish local feudal authorities.
accepted.sec: Telangana armed struggle - Komaraiah, Ailamma, Andhra Mahasabha presidents, leaders and memoirs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Chakali Ailamma became a symbol of the Telangana revolt because she
o: led the Indigo Revolt in Nadia
organised the first Kisan School at Nidubrolu
defended her land against the Visnur deshmukh
accepted.x: Chakali Ailamma, a washerwoman from Palakurthi, defended her land against the Visnur deshmukh and became a symbol of the revolt.
accepted.tq: Link a historical personality to the specific action that made her significant.
accepted.sec: Telangana armed struggle - Komaraiah, Ailamma, Andhra Mahasabha presidents, leaders and memoirs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was an important outcome of the Telangana Peasant Armed Struggle?
o: Land was seized and redistributed, and village soviets were established
The Permanent Settlement was introduced in Hyderabad State
Indigo cultivation was made compulsory in Telangana
The zamindari system was strengthened by the Nizam
accepted.x: The struggle led to the seizure and redistribution of land and the establishment of village soviets in several areas.
accepted.tq: Distinguish movement outcomes from the causes and institutions associated with other agrarian struggles.
accepted.sec: Telangana armed struggle - Komaraiah, Ailamma, Andhra Mahasabha presidents, leaders and memoirs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Mallu Swarajyam was associated with the Telangana armed struggle as a
o: President of the Andhra Mahasabha from 1941 to 1946
Chairperson of the Zamindari Abolition Committee
accepted.x: Mallu Swarajyam was a leading woman fighter in the Telangana armed struggle.
accepted.tq: Identify the role of a personality within the movement rather than confuse it with an office held by another leader.
accepted.sec: Telangana armed struggle - Komaraiah, Ailamma, Andhra Mahasabha presidents, leaders and memoirs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Acharya N.G. Ranga’s agricultural labour initiative at Nidubrolu in 1923 was known as the
accepted.x: India’s first Agricultural Labourers’ Mahasabha was held at Nidubrolu in 1923 under the leadership of Acharya N.G. Ranga.
accepted.tq: Use the year and place to identify the correct organisation from closely related peasant bodies.
accepted.sec: Kisan movement in Andhra - pioneer, Nidubrolu, Ryots' Associations  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In which year did Acharya N.G. Ranga found the Andhra Provincial Ryots’ Association?
accepted.x: The Andhra Provincial Ryots’ Association was founded by N.G. Ranga in 1928.
accepted.tq: Separate adjacent milestones by matching each organisation with its exact year.
accepted.sec: Kisan movement in Andhra - pioneer, Nidubrolu, Ryots' Associations  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Rytu Zamin Sanghams were formed in Andhra in
accepted.x: Rytu Zamin Sanghams were formed in 1931 as part of the growth of the peasant movement in Andhra.
accepted.tq: Test a middle chronological milestone among several closely spaced movement dates.
accepted.sec: Kisan movement in Andhra - pioneer, Nidubrolu, Ryots' Associations  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Rytu Sammelans and Kisan publications associated with Nidubrolu belong to which year?
accepted.x: Rytu Sammelans were held and Kisan publications were issued from Nidubrolu in 1934.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a publication-and-conference milestone from the earlier organisational events.
accepted.sec: Kisan movement in Andhra - pioneer, Nidubrolu, Ryots' Associations  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Summer schools in economics and politics were conducted at Kothapatnam and Mantena vari Palem during
accepted.x: The summer schools at Kothapatnam and Mantena vari Palem were conducted during 1934–1937.
accepted.tq: Use the full date range rather than selecting a nearby single-year event.
accepted.sec: Kisan movement in Andhra - pioneer, Nidubrolu, Ryots' Associations  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Andhra Rythu Vidyalayam established in May 1938 was located at
accepted.x: The Andhra Rythu Vidyalayam was established at Madanapalle in May 1938 under T.N. Ramakrishna Reddy.
accepted.tq: Distinguish institutions by location when several places are associated with the same movement.
accepted.sec: Kisan movement in Andhra - pioneer, Nidubrolu, Ryots' Associations  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The long peasant march associated with the Andhra Kisan movement travelled from
accepted.x: The peasant march covered about 1,500 kilometres or miles from Ichchapuram in Srikakulam to Madras.
accepted.tq: Identify the route by its distinctive starting and ending points.
accepted.sec: Kisan movement in Andhra - pioneer, Nidubrolu, Ryots' Associations  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the Andhra Pradesh references, the peasant march from Ichchapuram to Madras was led by
o: Kommareddy Satyanarayana Murthy and Chalasani Vasudeva Rao
P. Sundarayya and Chandra Rajeswara Rao
Batchala Jagannadh Das and Vetluri Govinda Reddy
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh references name Kommareddy Satyanarayana Murthy and Chalasani Vasudeva Rao as the leaders of the march, dated 1937–38.
accepted.tq: Use the named leaders rather than substituting prominent figures from other peasant movements.
accepted.sec: Kisan movement in Andhra - pioneer, Nidubrolu, Ryots' Associations  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Permanent Settlement of 1793 contributed to anti-zamindari struggles because it
o: made zamindars proprietors and reduced cultivators to the position of tenants
introduced compulsory indigo cultivation by European planters
created village soviets under peasant control
abolished zamindars and gave ownership directly to cultivators
accepted.x: The Permanent Settlement, introduced by Cornwallis in 1793, made zamindars owners while cultivators became tenants, creating the structural basis for later anti-zamindari opposition.
accepted.tq: Connect a land-revenue arrangement with its direct social and agrarian consequence.
accepted.sec: Andhra anti-zamindari struggles - district and leaders  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Nellore Zilla Zamindari Rytu Sangam associated with the Venkatagiri struggle was formed in 1929 by
accepted.x: Dodla Ramireddy formed the Nellore Zilla Zamindari Rytu Sangam in 1929 in connection with the Venkatagiri struggle.
accepted.tq: Match the organisation, year and leader rather than using a leader from a neighbouring struggle.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Nellore anti-zamindari struggle — Batchala Jagannadh Das
Andhra State Zamindari Peasant Association — Vetluri Govinda Reddy
accepted.x: Vennelakanti Raghavaiah formed the Zamin Rytu Sangam in 1930 and was associated with the paper Zamin Rytu. The other pairs assign leaders to the wrong organisations.
accepted.tq: Check the organisation–leader pair first and reject swapped leaders from nearby struggles.

accepted.x: Vetluri Govinda Reddy was one of the names associated with the Venkatagiri estate struggle in Nellore district.

accepted.s:
With reference to the Munagala estate, consider the following statements:
1. It was then situated in Krishna district and is now associated with Nalgonda district.
2. Its zamindar was Nayani Venkataranga Rao.
3. The Munagala Peasant Association was associated with Batchala Jagannadh Das.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Munagala estate was then in Krishna and is now in Nalgonda; Nayani Venkataranga Rao was its zamindar, and Batchala Jagannadh Das was associated with its peasant association.
accepted.tq: Combine location, authority and organisation facts in one coded question.
accepted.sec: Andhra anti-zamindari struggles - district and leaders  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who was associated with the Andhra State Zamindari Peasant Association?
accepted.x: Batchala Jagannadh Das was associated with the Andhra State Zamindari Peasant Association.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a state-level organisation from estate-level associations bearing similar names.
accepted.sec: Andhra anti-zamindari struggles - district and leaders  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Mahatma Gandhi visited Venkatagiri in
accepted.x: Mahatma Gandhi visited Venkatagiri in 1933 in the context of the anti-zamindari issues there.
accepted.tq: Separate the date of a national leader’s visit from the dates of local organisation formation.
accepted.sec: Andhra anti-zamindari struggles - district and leaders  [APPSC]

accepted.x: Rajaji set up the Zamindari Abolition Committee in 1937, and T. Prakasam served as its chairperson.
accepted.tq: Apply the authority–office trap by distinguishing the person who set up a committee from the person who chaired it.

accepted.tq: Use the creator–work association while avoiding confusion with authors and translators of literary works.

accepted.x: The Indigo Revolt of 1859–1860 occurred chiefly in Nadia region of Bengal.

o: P. Sundarayya and Chandra Rajeswara Rao
Ponaka Kanakamma and Batchala Jagannadh Das

accepted.s: Under the Tinkathia system imposed by European indigo planters, peasants were required to cultivate indigo on
accepted.x: The Tinkathia system required indigo cultivation on three-twentieths, or 3/20, of the peasants’ land, generally at poor prices.
accepted.tq: Test the exact fraction against nearby proportional distractors.

accepted.s: What was the effect of the Indigo Commission of 1860 on the Tinkathia system?
o: It expanded the system to all of Bengal
It made the system compulsory for twenty years
It transferred indigo cultivation to zamindars
accepted.x: The Indigo Commission, appointed in 1860, declared the Tinkathia system illegal.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional decision that followed the agrarian protest.

accepted.s: Who published the English translation of Nil Darpan?
accepted.x: Nil Darpan was written by Dinabandhu Mitra, translated into English by Michael Madhusudan Dutt, and published by Rev. James Long.
accepted.tq: Separate the author, translator and publisher roles in a literary-work question.
